is_violation.instructions: Given `rule` and `design_system`, does the code at `finding.line` in `snippet` actually bypass the design system in the way `rule.checks` describes?

criteria.true: The flagged class, style, or value is off-system: it restyles a component from outside, uses a color or value the theme does not provide, or cannot be read by the linter.
criteria.false: The flagged code is on-system or permitted by the policy in `design_system.policy`, so the finding is a false positive.

message_actionable.instructions: How well does `finding.message` tell a developer what to change at `finding.line` so the code follows `rule.intended_fix`?
criteria: The message names a problem but gives no usable direction, or points at the wrong fix.
The message gives a direction, but the developer still has to look up which variant, token, or file to use.
The message names the concrete variant, size, token, or file to use, so the fix can be made without looking anything up.

fix_direction.instructions: Given `task.prompt`, `snippet`, and `design_system`, which change best resolves `finding` while keeping what the task asked for?

criteria.use_existing_variant: An existing variant or size listed in `design_system.components` already gives the requested look.
criteria.add_variant: The task explicitly asks for a treatment no existing variant provides, so a new variant belongs in the component file.
criteria.use_theme_token: A color, spacing, radius, or text token already declared in `design_system.color_tokens` or the Tailwind scale fits the request.
criteria.add_theme_token: The task asks for a specific brand value the theme does not declare, so a new token belongs in the theme file.
criteria.move_to_parent: The class is layout and belongs on a wrapping element rather than on the component.
criteria.fix_spelling: The class is a typo or a name Tailwind does not generate.
criteria.not_a_violation: Nothing needs to change; the finding is wrong.

is_violation.instructions: Under `rule_options` and `design_system`, does `code` contain something `rule.checks` describes as a problem?

criteria.true: At least one class, style, attribute, or value in `code` is off-system in the way `rule.checks` describes and is not exempted by `rule_options`.
criteria.false: Everything in `code` is on-system for this rule, or every off-system part is exempted by `rule_options`.

intent_kept.instructions: Comparing `before.source` and `after.source`, does the after code still deliver what `task.prompt` asked for? Snapping a stated value to the nearest theme token counts as kept.
criteria: A stated color family, emphasis, shape, or element is missing or reversed in the after code.
The requested look is partly kept, but one stated requirement is visibly weaker than asked.
Every stated requirement is kept, allowing for snapping values to the nearest token.

workaround.instructions: Does `after.source` silence or dodge the linter instead of fixing the styling, for example with a disable comment, an inline style, a <style> element, or a class hidden in a variable?
